Works with

Rugged tablets for the Totalmobile Mobile Working app (Mobilise)

Totalmobile is a UK field service and mobile workforce management platform, headquartered in Belfast and sold as the Field First platform. The vendor lists sectors including local government, social housing, housing associations and housing contractors, facilities management, health and social care, utilities and telecoms, and names organisations such as Sheffield City Council, Southampton City Council, SNG, Bromford Flagship LiveWest, Fortem and Morgan Sindall Property Services on its site.

The operative-facing part is the Mobile Working capability, which the vendor's documentation library lists as Mobile Working (Mobilise). It is installed as the Totalmobile app, which the vendor describes as supported by iOS, Android and Windows devices or operating systems. Staff see assigned work in a job calendar or map view, follow pre-approved workflows, and capture data through forms with drop-down menus, photographs, voice recordings, free text and signatures. The vendor states the app has full offline capability, with critical job information stored locally on the device and updates syncing when connectivity is restored.

A consumer tablet carried in and out of vans, lofts, plant rooms and tenants' homes is more likely to crack, run flat or fail in rain and cold than to be replaced because its software is out of date. This page sets out what Totalmobile publishes about its app's platform requirements, which Tuga devices meet those published requirements, and what cannot be verified because the vendor does not publish it.

Requirements

What Totalmobile (Field First platform and the Totalmobile Mobile Working app, also called Mobilise) needs from a device

Each item below comes from TotalMobile Solutions Ltd's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android app from Google Play

    The Totalmobile app (package com.totalmobile, developer TotalMobile Solutions Ltd) is published on Google Play. When checked on 12 October 2026 the listing did not display a Requires Android label, so the minimum Android version is unverified. Check the current listing in the Play app before relying on a figure. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 and the A6 runs Android 15. Source: play.google.com

  • Windows app from the Microsoft Store

    The Totalmobile app for Windows (product ID 9WZDNCRCWSN4, publisher TotalMobile Solutions Limited) lists Windows 10 version 14393.0 or higher on x86, x64 or Arm, available on PC, Mobile and Surface Hub. The store notes add that Totalmobile for Windows v8 and later requires Windows 10 1709. Listed features are visits, forms, bulletins, homescreen and map my day. Source: apps.microsoft.com

  • Offline working

    The Mobile Working page states full offline capability, with all critical job information stored locally on the device, no dependency on signal, and updates syncing automatically when connectivity is restored. The Asset Management page also lists offline working alongside photo documentation and signature capture. The vendor's G-Cloud 15 listing on the UK Digital Marketplace adds that offline mobile capability may limit some features until connectivity is restored. Source: totalmobile.com

  • Camera and touchscreen for data capture

    Smart forms offer drop-down menus, photographs, voice recordings and free text, and staff capture signatures and photos on site. The Windows app's store listing declares webcam and microphone permissions. A device therefore needs a usable rear camera and a touchscreen for signatures, and voice recording needs a working microphone; check voice capture on a trial unit with your own configured forms. Source: totalmobile.com

  • Location for map view

    Staff view assigned work through a job calendar or map view, and the Windows store listing declares a location permission. A device with GPS makes the map view and location features usable away from Wi-Fi. Source: apps.microsoft.com

  • Mobile data for sync between jobs

    The vendor says field teams can complete work digitally from their mobile device, online or offline, with updates syncing when connectivity is restored. A tablet with a SIM slot keeps the day's jobs updating between visits rather than waiting for depot Wi-Fi. Source: totalmobile.com

  • Browser for the back office

    The 2025 Field First platform brochure describes the platform as SaaS with cloud-based hosting, and the vendor's G-Cloud 15 listing states that the service has a web browser interface (Microsoft Edge, Chrome and Safari) and that the desktop service provides the full back-office environment for planners, managers and administrators, while the mobile service is built for frontline field workers. Supervisors who need both will want a device with a full desktop browser. Source: applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk

  • NFC permission on Windows (feature not documented)

    The Windows store listing declares the permission to use devices that support Near Field Communication services. The vendor does not document what NFC is used for, and no barcode, QR or RFID feature is described on the vendor site, in the 2025 platform brochure or in any store listing. Do not buy on the assumption that these features exist in the app. Source: apps.microsoft.com

Totalmobile also publishes a Windows app in the Microsoft Store, and its G-Cloud listing describes a web browser interface for the back-office desktop service. For teams standardised on Windows, or supervisors who need the operative app and the browser-based admin tools on one device, the Tuga W10 runs Windows 11 Pro on an Intel N100 (x64), a later OS than the Windows 10 version 14393.0 the store lists and one of its listed architectures. It adds RJ45 Ethernet, HDMI and USB-A for depot use. Its IP65 rating is for dust and water jets, not immersion, and its removable 5000mAh battery is smaller than the Android devices' batteries, so real run time depends on load. The Windows store notes refer to an October 2024 9.27 release while the Android app is at 9.42.9, so confirm with Totalmobile that the Windows app is supported for your deployment.

  • Windows app requirement of Windows 10 version 14393.0 or higher on x86, x64 or Arm: the W10 runs Windows 11 Pro on an Intel N100 up to 3.4GHz (x64), with 8GB RAM and 128GB storage.
  • Browser-based back office: a full desktop browser on a 10.1 inch 1280 x 800 multi-touch IPS screen, with HDMI for an external monitor.
  • Photographs: 5MP rear camera and 2MP front camera for the webcam permission the store listing declares.
  • NFC permission declared by the Windows app: the W10 includes NFC hardware. What the app does with NFC is not documented by the vendor.
  • Depot and vehicle use: 100Mbps RJ45 Ethernet, USB-C, USB-A, pogo pin dock connector, optional 4G LTE and GPS, removable 5000mAh battery, IP65, 1197g.

Worth knowing. Totalmobile publishes no supported-device list, hardware minimums or screen-size guidance. The public home page of its documentation library at docs.totalmobile.com lists product names only, and the product documentation behind it requires a login, so nothing on this page is a vendor recommendation. The Android app's minimum Android version could not be read from the Play listing and should be checked in the Play app before purchase. Barcode, QR, NFC and RFID features are not documented anywhere by the vendor; the only evidence is an NFC permission declared by the Windows app. If your forms are configured to scan codes, that would most likely be camera-based through the app; the Tuga A10 has no dedicated scan engine, and the A6's built-in Zebra 2D scan engine has no documented Totalmobile use (the W10 offers an optional 2D barcode scanner and optional UHF RFID reader, but no Totalmobile feature using them is documented either). The W10 is IP65 and not rated for immersion, and its 5000mAh battery is not an all-day battery under heavy use. Neither the A10 nor the A6 lists a fingerprint reader, which matters if your organisation uses the app's optional fingerprint sign-in. The Android app's Play rating was 3.1 from 104 reviews on 12 October 2026, which is a comment on the software rather than any device.
Setting up

Getting Totalmobile (Field First platform and the Totalmobile Mobile Working app, also called Mobilise) running

  1. Confirm with your Totalmobile administrator which platform your organisation deploys and obtain the site address, instance name and user credentials for your organisation. Totalmobile is deployed per organisation, so devices are set up under your existing contract rather than through a public sign-up.
  2. Install the app: on the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, open Google Play, search for Totalmobile (developer TotalMobile Solutions Ltd, package com.totalmobile) and install. On the Tuga W10, open the Microsoft Store and install Totalmobile (product ID 9WZDNCRCWSN4).
  3. Activate with the details your administrator issued and grant the permissions the app requests. The Windows listing declares location, webcam, microphone, home or work network, internet and NFC permissions; photographs, voice recordings and the map view depend on these.
  4. Run the first sync on Wi-Fi or mobile data before the operative leaves the depot, then check that assigned jobs are visible with the device in flight mode to confirm the offline capability the vendor describes.
  5. If your IT team uses mobile device management, enrol the tablet before handing it over, and insert the SIM in the A10, A8 or A6 (or specify the optional 4G LTE module when ordering the W10) so jobs sync between visits.
  6. Fit the vehicle mounting dock in the van or a charging dock at the depot, and add a tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out. The A10 ships with a hand strap in the box.
